text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-The government has rejected a request from the state competition agency to intervene against what the watchdog perceives as discrimination against customers by some electricity companies.
-The tax payers' association says planning minister Terje Roed-Larsen's profit of 600,000 crowns from selling a share option in 1987 should have been taxed as ordinary income.
-The justice ministry says Palestinian hijacker Souhaila Andrawes may serve her 12-year sentence in Norway. She was sentenced yesterday by a German court.
--The profits of Scandinavian Airlines System are in a free fall.
- Kjell Inge Roekke's investment group RGI will gain the most from the proposed merger with offshore engineering and building materials group Aker.
-A tax issue could stop the planned merger between RGI and Aker.
-Brokerhouse Fondsfinans is sceptical to the planned merger between RGI and Aker. A confidential analysis questions RGI's cashflow and what it says is risk and a lack of information from the company.
-Insurance group Storebrand, which owns three percent of Aker stock, says it will vote in favour of the proposed merger between Aker and RGI at a shareholders' meeting on Thursday.
